root_idea.summary: An expressive vocalization of pain, grief, or feeling, reflected in the exclamation “Ah!” and extended to repeated moaning, compassion, and earnest supplication.
root_idea.development: The evidence treats this as an expressive word rather than a root yielding a general analogical principle. Its semantic development runs from the exclamation and moan to the descriptive epithet أَوَّاه for one marked by compassion or devotional pleading.

senses.definition: Compassionate and tender-hearted; moved by pity for others.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic descriptive epithet for a person characterized by compassionate concern. It accounts for the compassionate interpretation of the form in the passage concerning Abraham.

senses.definition: One who earnestly supplicates God; imploring and devout in prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic devotional use, including the interpretation of أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ as a believing supplicant. The sense emphasizes persistent, humble calling upon God rather than a mere vocal expression of pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moan, utter a prolonged complaint, or express pain and distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V verb; equivalent in the cited lexical discussion to expressing or experiencing pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who frequently says “Ah!” or moans, especially in grief, sorrow, lamentation, or complaint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the person-denoting extension of the exclamation. The utterance may also arise from affection, pity, compassion, or impatience; those illustrative motives do not impose an object-class restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exclamation meaning “Ah!” or “alas!”, expressing pain, grief, sorrow, lamentation, complaint, or moaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used with مِنْ, لِ, or عَلَى to indicate the cause or object of the complaint. It can also express pity, compassion, or impatience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry addressed to horses to make them return.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized imperative-like animal call, distinct from the exclamation expressing human grief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A moan or act of moaning; also an imprecation wishing moaning upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may stand for the verbal action of moaning and occurs in the imprecatory expression آهَةً لَكَ or its variant أَوَّةً لَكَ.
A rare technical usage attested in an imprecation pairing measles with smallpox.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One frequent in prayer, praise, or glorification of God, or one who often invites to what is good; also reported for a believer or a person skilled in religious law.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are broader Classical Arabic devotional and descriptive extensions of the epithet, distinct from the specifically Quran-attested compassionate and supplicating uses listed above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who says “Ah!” or “alas!”, or who abases himself in earnest supplication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of a person characterized by moaning or humble supplication.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Defines the Form V verb as moaning or expressing pain.
Defines the exclamation and its specialized use as a horse-return call.
Defines آهَة as a moan and in an imprecation.
Contains the Quran-attested compassionate and supplicating branches and broader moaning and devotional extensions.
Defines مُتَأَوِّه as one who says Ah or abases himself in supplication.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation notation and are not treated as modern surah:ayah locations; the examples here use the independently supplied QAC locations.

The supplied contextual renderings vary between “compassionate” and “imploring.” The broader meaning of frequent moaning is retained as Classical Arabic evidence rather than assigned as a separate Quranic sense because the packet does not securely tie that interpretation to a specific supplied QAC occurrence.
